page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized instance provisioned with 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 4 physical Intel cores with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 16.0 GB, providing an allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache. Supported instruction sets encompass Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX-512, VNNI, BF16), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile, int8), as well as hardware cryptographic instructions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs.

Performance testing across standard benchmarks places the processor within average performance bands. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 7215.0 and a single-core score of 1877.0. Stress-ng multi-core testing resulted in 7217.53, while software compilation via Clang reached 8701.0. Advanced instruction support yields PassMark extended instruction scores of 9025.06 and encryption scores of 7015.39. Cached memory bandwidth reaches 568.81 GB/sec, dropping to 68.85 GB/sec read and 40.33 GB/sec write for uncached 256MB blocks. A key hardware tradeoff is memory throughput, where PassMark memory benchmarks scored in the weak percentile. Additionally, while small 135M parameter LLM inference runs comfortably at 219.21 tokens/sec, text generation on a 7B model drops to 7.92 tokens/sec.

The high ratio of compute cores to memory provides resource efficiency for CPU-intensive workloads that do not demand extensive RAM capacity. Workloads utilizing specialized matrix or vector operations benefit directly from integrated Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions without requiring standalone GPU accelerators. The instance delivers steady performance for software compilation, build systems, CI/CD pipelines, web serving throughput up to 11.89 GB/sec, and light database operations like Redis key-value processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual server featuring 8 dedicated x86_64 Intel vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 16.0 GB of RAM. The architecture delivers 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU alongside 260 MB of L3 cache and support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. Benchmark evaluations place CPU performance in average tiers, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 7215.0 and PassMark CPU score of 12045.57. Memory testing reveals reduced bandwidth under heavy uncached loads, scoring in lower percentiles for PassMark memory. Storage is not bundled locally, and no GPU hardware is attached. The compute-dense architecture offers cost-effective execution for CPU-bound tasks that do not require high memory footprints. It is well suited for software compilation, CI/CD build environments, web serving, and small-scale machine learning inference.
